title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is dated 26 June 1986 and opens 'Analysis situs (quatrième mouture)', section I: 'Récapitulation en termes de magasins'. It sets up an order-theoretic axiomatics meant to carry Grothendieck's late programme of 'tame' or 'moderate' topology (cf. Esquisse d'un programme §5–6). He calls the algebraic formalism of an 'algebra of multistructures' a 'magasin'.

A magasin is a set M with three relations: ≤, ≪ and |o|.
- Mag1: ≤ and ≪ are partial orders, and X ≤ Y ⇒ X ≪ Y.
- Notation: X̃ := M_{≤X} = {Y | Y ≤ X}, the principal lower set.
- Mag2: if X ≪ Y, the set Ỹ^X = {Z ≤ Y | X ≪ Z} has a ≤-smallest element. This is a 'carrier' or 'support' of X inside Y. One writes X ≪̊ Y when this carrier is Y itself, i.e. X sits 'generically' or 'in the interior' of Y.
- Mag3: |o| is symmetric and antireflexive. Moreover X|o|Y, X' ≪̊ X, Y' ≪̊ Y ⇒ X'|o|Y'. So 'disjointness' passes to pieces lying in the open part.
- Mag4: distinct elements below a common X are |o|-related.

The intended model is visible from the axioms:
- elements of M are strata or cells of a stratified tame object;
- X ≤ Y means 'X is a stratum of the canonical stratification of the closure of Y' (a face relation);
- ≪ is a coarser incidence or inclusion relation;
- |o| means 'disjoint' (as open strata).
Mag4 then says the strata of a single closed cell are pairwise disjoint.

Two definitions follow.
- X ≭ Y (compatibility, despite the crossed symbol): every stratum of X̃ not in X̃∩Ỹ is |o|-disjoint from every stratum of Ỹ not in X̃∩Ỹ. In other words, the two closed cells meet only along common faces, as cells of a complex must.
- X ∥ Y: all strata of X̃ and Ỹ are pairwise disjoint (disjoint closures).
- The stated consequence is X ∥ Y ⇔ (X ≭ Y and X̃∩Ỹ = ∅, i.e. {X,Y} has no common ≤-lower bound).

The next page uses this to define 'figures' as ≤-closed subsets that are pairwise compatible. These are abstract complexes, with an optional 'polyhedral' condition that pairwise meets exist. The embedding X ↦ X̃ sends M into its figures, with ≤ extended as inclusion. The page is thus the axiomatic base for a purely combinatorial or order-theoretic 'analysis situs' of stratified spaces.
errors: No mathematical error found. The equivalence X∥Y ⇔ (X≭Y and X̃∩Ỹ=∅) is correct. If Z ∈ X̃∩Ỹ, then X∥Y would force Z|o|Z, which antireflexivity forbids. Conversely, if the intersection is empty, the two definitions coincide.

Small consistency remarks, not errors. Mag1+Mag2 give X ≪̊ X, and for X' ≤ X the carrier of X' in X̃ is X' itself, so X' ≪̊ X with X' ≤ X forces X' = X. Mag3b is therefore genuinely about ≪-incidences that are not ≤-incidences, as intended.

The axioms are a 'récapitulation' and are evidently provisional. A marginal note says some axioms (ABC?) are moved to or replaced by an older axiom 'A4'. Nothing guarantees here that the axiom set is complete for the intended stratified models.

ideas.what: 'Magasin': a set with two compatible partial orders (≤ ⊂ ≪) and a symmetric antireflexive 'disjointness' relation, axiomatizing the strata or cells of tame stratified spaces.
ideas.modern_name: abstract cell complex / face poset of a stratification, with an incidence/disjointness structure; closest: abstract polyhedral complexes, posets of strata of stratified spaces, combinatorial side of o-minimal cell decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abstract cell complexes: Steinitz (1908), Tucker (1933), Kovalevsky (1989). Posets of strata: Whitney/Thom/Mather; MacPherson; Lurie (exit paths). Tame topology: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (1984–86).
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic idea of 'topologie modérée' appears, in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6. This specific axiomatics is unpublished as far as I know.

ideas.what: Carrier of X inside Y as the ≤-least element of {Z ≤ Y | X ≪ Z}, and the derived relation X ≪̊ Y ('X lies in the open part of Y').
ideas.modern_name: carrier / support face (smallest closed cell containing a point or subcell); open-star or interior incidence
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical combinatorial topology (carrier of a simplex/point: Alexandroff, Lefschetz)

ideas.what: Compatibility relation X ≭ Y (the closures meet only along common strata) and parallelism X ∥ Y (disjoint closures), with the equivalence X∥Y ⇔ X≭Y and no common lower bound.
ideas.modern_name: cells intersecting in a common subcomplex (condition defining a regular/polyhedral complex); disjoint closed cells

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck is building a purely order-theoretic axiomatics ('magasins', 'algèbres de multistructures') for his tame-topology analysis situs. It is in its fourth version ('quatrième mouture') and is meant to produce stratified 'figures' combinatorially rather than via o-minimal model theory. To my knowledge this framework was never published or taken up. The literature realized tame topology through o-minimality (van den Dries) instead.
missed.quote: J'appelle le formalisme algébrique d'une "algèbre de multistructures", un "magasin"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A specialist would value an alternative, model-theory-free combinatorial foundation of 'figures' in tame topology. It is relevant to current work on posets of strata, exit-path ∞-categories and constructible sheaves, and to combinatorial models of stratified spaces. It would also document how Grothendieck's own tame-topology programme concretely looked after the Esquisse.

missed.claim: The axioms, read with the next page's 'figures' (lower sets with pairwise compatible generators, plus a 'polyhedral' meet condition), amount to an abstract theory of cell or stratum posets. In that theory a stratified object is recovered from its poset together with an incidence/disjointness relation. This anticipates the later viewpoint that a (conical) stratified space is controlled by its poset of strata (MacPherson; Lurie HA App. A). Grothendieck does not make the link explicitly on this page.
missed.quote: La structure est celle d'un ens. M avec trois relations ≤, ≪, |o|
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing these axioms with modern face-poset/stratification characterizations (e.g. regular CW complexes via face posets, Björner) could show whether Grothendieck's ≪ / |o| data captures non-regular incidence. That information is not visible in the face poset alone.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a notable unpublished detail: the actual axioms of Grothendieck's 1986 'magasin' formalism for tame analysis situs. However, the mathematics on this page is elementary order-theoretic definition, close to standard abstract cell complex notions. Its interest is mainly historical and programmatic.
transcription_corrections: The symbol written '≭' (X ≭ Y) is a crossed relation sign used positively, meaning 'compatible' (the closures meet along common faces). It is not a negation; the next page uses it as the condition defining figures.
The Mag2 addition after 'admet un plus petit élément' is partly illegible. It seems to give a name or notation for this smallest element ('…, i.e. Ỹ^X …'); the '[?]' should be kept.
The marginal note on the left near Mag4 is very uncertain. It may read something like 'ABC est rédigé … l'ancien A4,3' rather than 'déplacé à l'axiome A4'.
The '8' at bottom left is an archive foliation number, not part of the text.
The header reads 'GF VIII' (possibly 'CF VIII'), and the cross-reference is 'cf GF VII, p. 110'.
